clue.text: Observes a western board game

parts.note: to observe something is to see it, so observes gives sees

explanation.surface: Someone watches a cowboy-themed board game being played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board game' is a playful definition: the plank on which children play up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a plank balanced on a pivot that children use for a back-and-forth playground pastime.

clue.text: Less so for the Duke of Plaza- Toro leading his regiment from behind

definitions.text: Less so for the Duke of Plaza- Toro leading his regiment from behind

parts.words: Less so for the Duke of Plaza- Toro leading his regiment from behind
parts.note: Gilbert and Sullivan's cowardly Duke led from the rear, as he found it less thrilling there

explanation.surface: A comic opera duke shirks the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's The Gondoliers the Duke 'led his regiment from behind: he found it less' thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke's song says leading from the rear was less thrilling, safely tamer than the front.

clue.text: Bench badly accommodated in a coach

indicators.note: accommodated in means held inside the coach word

parts.note: a stage is short for a stagecoach
ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A seat poorly fitted into a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bench' suggests a seat, but here it is a stand for casks; 'accommodated in' is the container signal, and STAGE is short for stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: A stillage is a stand or frame on which casks or goods are kept off the floor.

clue.text: Israel so named after a night of it

definitions.text: Israel so named after a night of it

parts.words: Israel so named after a night of it
parts.note: in Genesis Jacob grappled with an angel all night and was then renamed Israel

explanation.surface: A biblical renaming after a long night.
explanation.walkthrough: Genesis 32: Jacob struggles with an angel until dawn and is renamed Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob's all-night bout with the angel was a grappling contest, the sport of throwing an opponent.

clue.text: A number of sanctimonious Poles in the alley

parts.note: nine is a number
pi is crossword slang for pious or sanctimonious
N is the north pole
S is the south pole

explanation.surface: Some self-righteous Polish people are hanging about in a back lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' look like people from Poland, but they are the two magnetic poles, N and S. The definition is loose: ninepins is the game played in a skittle alley.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepins is skittles, a game played down a long lane called a skittle alley.

clue.text: Antonio's Italian variety of public ownership

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive's s counts here, giving all the letters of Antonios

explanation.surface: An Italian man's brand of state control.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking an industry into state control puts it under public rather than private ownership.

clue.text: Issue' shows a sirenian, but tail-first

indicators.note: tail-first means the last letter goes to the front

parts.note: a manatee is a sea cow, of the order Sirenia

explanation.surface: A sea cow appears backwards in a magazine edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail-first' moves MANATEE's last letter, E, to the front. Sirenians are the sea cows.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow out or come forth from a source.

clue.text: Sluggishness in W3 about lunch-time

indicators.note: about means going round, so the place name encloses the numeral

parts.note: W3 is the London postcode for Acton
lunch-time is one o'clock, I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Lazy staff in a London district around noon.
explanation.walkthrough: W3 is the postcode of Acton, a district of west London. 'about' puts I inside ACTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is a lack of activity, the same idea as idleness.

clue.text: Fellow on deck is not necessarily an officer

definitions.text: Fellow on deck is not necessarily an officer

parts.words: Fellow on deck is not necessarily an officer
parts.note: a companion aboard a vessel bears the title mate without being the officer called mate

explanation.surface: A sailor on board may not hold rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipmate is a fellow sailor on the same vessel; a mate is also a ship's officer.

clue.text: Yard chief ordered ten to the west

parts.note: OC, officer commanding, is the chief of a unit
Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters, houses the CID, the Criminal Investigation Department

indicators.note: ordered means arranged anew, so the letters of ten are shuffled

explanation.surface: A senior Scotland Yard officer sends ten men westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' turns TEN into ENT. Scotland Yard is the London police headquarters, whose detectives form the CID.
explanation.definitionFit: The Occident is the western part of the world, as opposed to the Orient in the east.

clue.text: Some reform a law in an African state

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A country in Africa is changing part of its legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked country in south-east Africa.

clue.text: Some heel employed in cloak-and-dagger work?.

explanation.surface: Footwear somehow involved in espionage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall thin shoe heel takes the name of a slender dagger, a weapon of assassins and spies.

clue.text: Lighter than a feather, this fowl?

explanation.surface: A bird so slight it weighs less than one of its own feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: In boxing the bantamweight class is lighter than featherweight.
explanation.definitionFit: The bantamweight boxing division sits below featherweight, and a bantam is a small breed of chicken.

clue.text: The direction of unmanned missiles

parts.note: steering rockets without pilots is done by an onboard control system; the word also means direction or advice

explanation.surface: How pilotless rockets are steered to target.
explanation.definitionFit: Guided missiles are steered by a control system, and the same word means direction or advice.

clue.text: Porcelain from a country town in Herts

parts.note: China is a country
Ware is a town in Hertfordshire, a county north of London

explanation.surface: Fine pottery sourced from a provincial English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is Hertfordshire, an English county just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinaware is a general term for porcelain dishes and crockery.

clue.text: Uncle Sam's exclamation on seeing the moulding?

explanation.surface: An American gasps in admiration at some fancy plasterwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Oh gee is an American cry of surprise; an S-shaped architectural curve has a name that sounds the same.

clue.text: Spectator satisfactory in' no role, confound it

indicators.note: in puts the satisfactory word inside no role
confound means throw into confusion, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: OK means satisfactory

explanation.surface: A bystander is fine with having no part, but curses about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confound it' reads as an oath in the surface but signals the anagram; 'in' is the container signal applied before shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker watches events without taking part.

clue.text: Former wife modelling, in the nude?

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
posing is what an artist's model does

explanation.surface: An ex-wife poses naked for an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: one modelling in the nude is exposing all.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncovering the body for view is baring all, as an unclothed model does.

clue.text: Bet Alighieri's beheaded!

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter of the poet's name is cut off

parts.note: Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A wager that the Italian poet has lost his head.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a stake put into the pot in poker before the cards are dealt.

clue.text: A curse, having them in an anti-aircraft enclosure

indicators.note: enclosure means the anti-aircraft letters surround the word them

explanation.surface: Someone swears at enemies trapped in a gun emplacement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosure' reads as a gun pit but is the container signal; 'having' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal curse or ban pronounced by a church.

clue.text: Bond's 2 exploits so affected us

parts.note: the spy stories about Bond were exciting (the answer to 2), stirring readers

explanation.surface: James Bond's adventures moved the readers.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' refers to the answer to 2 Down, EXCITING.
explanation.definitionFit: Exciting adventures leave readers delighted and stirred.

clue.text: Sort of key to internal combustion

definitions.text: Sort of key to internal combustion

parts.words: Sort of key to internal combustion
parts.note: the key turned to start a car engine, which is what sets the fuel burning

explanation.surface: The secret of how engines burn fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's starter key switches on the spark system that fires the engine.

clue.text: Form of aid sent as an alternative

indicators.note: a form of something is a new shape, so the letters of aid sent are rearranged

explanation.surface: Help dispatched as a substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead means in place of something else.

clue.text: A player, one in odd boots

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the jumbled letters
odd means strange or irregular, so the letters of boots are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A footballer wearing mismatched boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' turns BOOTS into OBOST, and 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist plays the oboe, so is a musical performer.

clue.text: Riot backed by a striker in the slaughterhouse

parts.note: a bat is what strikes the ball

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so riot is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A violent disturbance at an abattoir, led by a worker on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests a worker on strike, but it is a cricket or baseball bat; 'backed' signals the reversal, giving TOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An abattoir is a place where animals are killed for meat.

clue.text: Bill for an emperor.?

parts.note: Bill is the nickname, as in ... Bill, given in Britain to Wilhelm II of Germany

explanation.surface: An invoice sent to an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Kaiser Bill was the British nickname for Germany's Wilhelm II.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaiser is the German title for an emperor.

clue.text: Claudio's sister, or the Pot of Basil

explanation.surface: Two literary heroines named side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Measure for Measure the nun pleading for Claudio is his sister; Keats's poem about the pot of basil bears the same heroine's name.

clue.text: Dance in progress after Latvian party.

indicators.note: after places the words in progress behind the rest

parts.note: Riga is the Latvian capital
a do is a party
something going on is in progress

explanation.surface: Dancing is underway following a reception in the Baltic.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigadoon is a lively old Provençal folk dance for couples.

clue.text: Grazers in Africa and in the Spanish quarter

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Animals feed in Africa and in a Spanish neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter' looks like a district of a city, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Elands are large African antelopes that feed on grass and leaves.
